u0: The agent is all caught up: no client is waiting to give an order, no taken order is awaiting service, and no dropped food needs immediate recovery. No requirement is currently outstanding, but the task is ongoing, so a new client arrival, a newly taken order, or a food slip will create fresh obligations. The agent may move around freely until then, and the standing duties apply again as soon as anything happens.
u1: An order has been taken and is still waiting to be served. The agent must obtain and prepare food as needed and then serve that client; until service is complete, this duty remains open. If food slips, it must be picked up on the very next step or the task fails. Since the shop allows only one client at a time, the next arrival comes only after this client is served, so finishing the current service is the priority.
u2: Food has just slipped from the agent's hands, and no client order is currently pending. The agent must be holding food again on the very next step; failing to recover it then permanently fails the task. Once the food is back in hand, no other obligation remains, and the agent can return to handling new clients or slips.
u3: Food has just slipped while an order has already been taken and is waiting to be served. The agent must be holding food on the very next step to recover the slip; otherwise the task fails for good. After recovering the food, the taken order still needs to be prepared and served, and any further slip must again be recovered immediately.
u4: A client is waiting at the counter and has not yet had their order taken. The agent must take that order, then fetch and prepare food and serve the client. No earlier order is pending service. If food slips in the meantime, it must be picked up on the very next step.
u5: A client is waiting to order, and food has just slipped from the agent's hands. The agent must be holding food again on the very next step; missing that permanently fails the task. After the food is recovered, the waiting client's order still needs to be taken and then served with prepared food, so both duties remain open.
u6: An order has already been taken and is still awaiting service, and a client is also waiting to have their order taken. Both order duties are outstanding: the agent must eventually serve the taken order and take the waiting client's order, then serve that one as well, fetching and preparing food as needed. If food slips, it must be recovered on the very next step.
u7: A client is waiting to order, an order has already been taken but not served, and food has just slipped. The agent must recover the food by holding food on the very next step, or the task fails immediately. After that, both order duties remain: take the waiting client's order and serve the earlier order, with food fetched and prepared as needed.
u8: A mandatory requirement has been broken beyond repair: food slipped and the agent was not holding food on the very next step, so the required immediate pickup was missed. Because that rule is failed for good, successful completion of the task is no longer possible. The agent may keep acting in the shop, but this failure cannot be undone.
